result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.degree_pearson_correlation_coefficient()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the Pearson correlation of degrees at either end of an edge. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19830-L19889){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.degree_pearson_correlation_coefficient( x="out", y="in", weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Degree Pearson correlation](/assets/graphs/degree-pearson-correlation-coefficient.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The hub-and-leaf graph with each degree in a badge. Over the ten edge ends the mean degree is 2.2; the degrees at the two ends of an edge have covariance -0.64 and variance 0.96, so their correlation is r = -0.667: hubs link to leaves." width="100%"} Degree assortativity measured as the Pearson correlation between the degrees of the two endpoints over all edges (Newman, 2002): positive when hubs link to hubs, negative when hubs link to low-degree nodes. On an undirected graph this equals `get_assortativity_degree()`; the directed `x=`/`y=` options choose which degree of the source and target to correlate (for example, out-degree of the source against in-degree of the target). Matches NetworkX's `degree_pearson_correlation_coefficient()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : On directed graphs, the degree of each edge's source: `"out"` (default) or `"in"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["in"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : On directed graphs, the degree of each edge's target: `"in"` (default) or `"out"`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether degrees are weighted. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The correlation coefficient in `[-1, 1]` (NaN if all degrees are equal). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A star is perfectly disassortative: ::: {#d7dd500c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ec.Graph().add_star_graph(5).degree_pearson_correlation_coefficient() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` -1.0 ``` ::: :::
